findings.trigger_condition: When processing a graph with many unhashable nodes
findings.root_cause: Unhashable node lookups use O(K) linear scan through the unhashable_nodes list. For K unhashable nodes with M edges, this results in O(K*M) time complexity which is O(N²) in the worst case.
findings.impact: Performance degrades quadratically with the number of unique unhashable nodes. Large graphs with unhashable nodes will be slow to process.
findings.suggested_validation: Benchmark with a graph containing 1000+ unique unhashable nodes (e.g., lists or custom objects without __hash__) and measure the time taken.

findings.trigger_condition: When processing equal hashable and unhashable node values across hashability boundaries
findings.root_cause: Hashable and unhashable nodes are tracked in completely separate data structures (hash_buckets dict vs unhashable_nodes list). Equal values that cross hashability boundaries (one hashable, one unhashable) are never compared for equality and get assigned different IDs.
findings.impact: Equal nodes treated as distinct nodes if they have different hashability. This breaks deduplication, layer assignment, and creates incorrect cycle detection.
findings.suggested_validation: Test with a custom class where some instances are hashable and some are not (e.g., by dynamically deleting __hash__ on some instances) but test equality across the hashability boundary.
